the confirmed misalignments are fixed and seen on screen before and after
crosscore_notes: All six cores load the save and draw every screen like mGBA. What is left: the title frame differs on every core because the intro animation runs at a different point when the save loads; on the main menu, the two buttons the game darkens with the GBA's brightness effect come out one step of the GBA's 5-bit colour apart; the start menu shows the time, and each core's clock started at a different second; and the bag's pocket arrows (VBA-M, VBA-Next, SkyEmu) and Mednafen-GBA's party icons are caught on another frame of their animation.

map_walk.held_reason: because the map starts a scripted Frontier or multi-battle sequence that the walker (which answers every prompt with B) cannot finish

known_issues_intro: The decisions behind the translation are in `translation/hebrew/DECISIONS.md` of the source fork.
known_issues: Ariana's class name מנהל רוקט is masculine because she shares the class with Archer, Proton, Petrel and Giovanni; other classes shared by men and women also keep the noun the trainer data gives them (DECISIONS.md Q124, Q127).

Battle Dome: a trainer's info card judges the team's battle style from a single move, so only three of its style descriptions ever appear: 'נכונות להסתכן מדי פעם באסון מוחלט.', 'שימוש במהלכים מפתיעים ומשבשים.' and 'שילוב מאוזן היטב של מהלכים.' English H&S 2.0.6 does the same ('Willing to risk total disaster at times.', 'Uses startling and disruptive moves.', 'Uses a well-balanced mix of moves.'); the other descriptions are translated but cannot appear.

Scott's Silver and Gold Shields, his prizes for 50 and 100 Battle Tower wins in a row, cannot be received: he offers each one and then always says to come back for it later. English H&S 2.0.6 does the same.

If the game finds no 128 KB Flash save (an emulator set to another save type, or a cart without a Flash chip), it first shows a blue English error screen ('OUT OF MEMORY TRYING TO ALLOCATE …'). Press START to see the Hebrew message, then set the save type to Flash 1M/128K and load the ROM again. The English 2.0.6 source built the same way shows the same screen.

Battle Pike: if the New Game option 'הישרדות מרעל' (Survive Poison) is off and poison makes the whole party faint while you walk in the Pike, the game crashes instead of ending the challenge. English H&S 2.0.6 does the same. The option is on by default.
Birth Island: answering YES when the sailor offers to sail you home crashes the game (black screen). English H&S 2.0.6 does the same. Save before you talk to him. Leave the island with Fly instead.

Saves from Heart & Soul before 2.0, such as 1.2.1, do not load, as in English H&S 2.0.6: the game says the save file was erased because of corruption or damage ('קובץ השמירה נמחק בגלל שיבוש או נזק.') and offers only a new game. Loading changes nothing in the file, but the first save of the new game does, so keep a copy of an old save. This was seen with a save built in the 1.2.1 layout; a real 1.2.1 save was not tried.
not_tested: Real hardware. No flashcart was available. The ROM is 32 MiB and needs a cart that supports 32 MiB images, with the save type set to FLASH 128 KB and a working RTC.
Playing by hand in a GUI. Every run above was automated. The tours type a Hebrew name and walk through menus and battles, but nobody played from a new game to the first badge.
A real 2.0.x save from a long playthrough. The save ladder was built with the harness and the debug menu.

Taking a save back to the English ROM from every place. Saves written by this ROM load in English 2.0.6 with no crash: a new-game save in the bedroom, whose bag and trainer card work; saves made in a Pokémon Center in the middle of the game and after the League, and saves made in a town, on a route and in a house, whose menus, party, bag, Pokédex, PokéGear and PC boxes look the same as with a save the English game wrote; a save made on a Trainer Hill floor during a challenge, after which the floor's tag battle, the trainers' lines and the stairs look the same too; and a save made on a Battle Pyramid floor, whose party, Pyramid bag and trainer card work. A Hebrew player name, and the name of a Pokémon the Hebrew game created, show blank in English. Saves made in other places, such as during another Battle Frontier challenge, were not tried.

A real link with a second GBA. The trade screen, link battles, the cable club and record-mixing lines and the Mystery Gift menus were seen on screen with the partner faked in memory. The Union Room and the wireless group screens need a Wireless Adapter and were not seen in play; the Union Room's trade board and its type list were drawn by forcing their state, with no letter cut off, and the rest of their strings passed the width audit only.

C strings no tour shows. A diagnostic build lists every translated C string the tours put on screen. The Pokédex entries and species names of Pokémon that only the randomizer brings into the game were shown on Pokédex pages filled in memory, which match the real caught pages pixel for pixel; a randomized new game was played to its first catches, but not every species was rolled. Not shown are 7 evolution-method words that the Pokédex evolution page never prints in H&S, about 35 lines that need a state the tours could not set up, and about 2,300 that H&S 2.0.6 cannot reach (link and wireless screens, switched-off features, Emerald and FireRed leftovers, unused data). Their widths were checked by the layout audit and by reviewers against the code, not on screen.
Female address. The player is addressed in the masculine throughout (a decision of this translation).
The randomizer and challenge options beyond their menus.

Easy Chat in full. The words and the ABC keyboard are Hebrew. Seen on screen: the four Day Care hint windows; the Odd Egg interview with its group keyboard, every key of the Hebrew ABC keyboard and every one of its 23 letter lists, the status, voices, feelings and actions lists and the YES/NO prompts; all eleven Odd Egg passwords giving their egg; the Battle Tower feelings man's start, win and loss screens; the contest and Battle Tower interviews, the apprentice's win speech and the mart questionnaire, opened with their script; writing mail from the bag and Kenya's mail; Battle Frontier and Battle Tent trainers' intros, win and loss lines; and the first Trainer Hill floor's trainer lines. Not seen: phrases that come from a linked game.
Cores other than the six listed, and RetroArch builds for Android or handhelds.

Most of the 525 item plural names. The bag, PC, Pyramid and mart count lines were seen on screen with a sample of them, the longest names and the widest counts; the rest were checked against the glossary rules and by tools/hebrew/plurals.py, which fails when a stackable item has no plural.

Names of Pokémon from Gen 4 on, and many trainer names, are transliterations marked "proposed" in the glossary. All 1,851 were reviewed against the transliteration rules, the official English pronunciation and consistency with related names, and 22 of the 23 changes it proposed were made (`translation/hebrew/DECISIONS.md`), but none was checked against an official Hebrew source or by a native speaker on screen. Every name was also compared with the FireRed translation's names and naming conventions and follows them, except where a limit of this game or a slip in FireRed stands in the way; each such name is listed with its reason (DECISIONS.md Q139, Q140); the Hoenn town and person names follow the FireRed translation where it prints them and the transliteration rules otherwise, and their 35 new names were reviewed the same way (Q141).

The new Psychic type name on the Union Room trade board in play, which needs a link; it was drawn there only by forcing the state. Every other place the new Psychic, Ghost and FireRed-convention names can appear was shown on screen, among them PSYCHIC GEM and PSYCHIC TERA SHARD in the PC storage and the battle debug menu's held-item effect name, or cannot be reached in this game, in English either: the Z-move panel, three Z-move and Max Move descriptions, the Kanto Pokémon Tower ghost, the AERODACTYL of Trainer Hill and Trainer Tower trainers, and the generic phrase for a Psychic move.

Wording read by a native speaker. Nobody whose first language is Hebrew has proofread the text on screen; reviewers asked for one on a few lines (the radio's adjective pairs, the Ultra Beast Pokédex entries, the Day Care take-back question).
